findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body:
`gen_request_data` merges errors into the breadcrumb stream by comparing `error_events[i]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore event data, which is float seconds (~1.7e9). The top-level `timestamp` on recorded replay events is in milliseconds (~1.7e12); the SDK writes breadcrumb custom events with `timestamp = breadcrumb.timestamp * 1000`.

Because of the unit mismatch, every error compares as "before" the first recording event. All error messages are emitted at the start of the log list instead of in chronological order. The log lines also carry inconsistent time units, which degrades the Seer summary.

The new tests mask this by using second-based timestamps for the recording events. Normalize both sides to the same unit before comparing, e.g. multiply the error timestamp by 1000.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes nodestore get_multi preserves input order
findings.body:
`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict. The base implementation fills it with cache hits first and then adds backend-fetched items, so the value order does not follow `node_ids`. Backends may also omit missing keys.

Zipping `error_ids` against `events.values()` can therefore attach the wrong event ID to an event's data, and can drop or shift entries when some IDs are missing.

Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

findings.title: All replay errors are injected into every paginated page
findings.body:
`analyze_recording_segments` is bound with the full `error_events` list and is called once per page of segments by `GenericOffsetPaginator`. `gen_request_data` yields any errors not consumed by the page's events at the end.

For replays spanning more than one page, every page's Seer request contains the complete set of errors, including errors outside that page's time range. Those errors are duplicated across pages and misattributed in the summaries.

Filter `error_events` to each page's time window, or fetch all segments in one request.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled
findings.body:
`query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` run unconditionally before the `enable_error_context` check. When the caller passes `enable_error_context=false`, the endpoint still pays for a Snuba round-trip whose result is discarded.

When error context is enabled, nodestore payloads for every error ID on the replay are fetched up front on each request.

Move the Snuba query inside the enabled branch.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered while a search query is active
findings.body:
The `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter is applied only in the branch after `if (!searchQuery.trim()) { return sorted; }`.

With an empty search box, the default view, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown. They disappear only once the user types a query.

Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the early return.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion checks for age/timestamp use truthiness
findings.body:
`validate_timestamp` uses `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` uses `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A value of 0 is falsy, and `age: 0` is common for freshly generated reports. A report carrying both `age: 0` and a `timestamp` therefore passes validation, contrary to the stated intent.

Neither field is required either, so a report with neither one is accepted, even though the docstrings say one must be present.

Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`, and add an object-level `validate()` that enforces exactly one of the two.

findings.title: One invalid report causes the whole batch to be rejected with 422
findings.body:
Browsers send reports in batches, and the Reporting API retries non-2xx deliveries. Returning 422 as soon as any single report fails validation drops all the valid reports in the same request.

The browser will then retry the entire batch, including the bad report that will never validate. That produces repeated failed deliveries and lost data for the valid reports.

Consider skipping or recording invalid reports individually and still returning 2xx.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization ignores the actual table results
findings.body:
When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, the loading state, field aliases and custom renderers.

Any org with the flag on sees an empty table for every table widget. Wire `result` into `tableData` and derive `columns` from `fields`, or keep the flag off until that is done.

findings.title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments
findings.body:
`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue in the comment. That method does a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, and `get_environment()` adds a DB lookup.

This runs serially inside the PR comment task for every issue listed, adding several round-trips per issue. Any failure is swallowed by a broad `except Exception`.

Consider batching the lookups or using a cheaper source of environment information, such as the group's tag values.

findings.title: Null max_segment_id case isn't actually exercised
findings.body:
The test now passes a row with `max_segment_id: None`, but `delete_matched_rows` is mocked. The new `None` guard in `_make_recording_filenames` is never executed.

If the guard were removed, this test would still pass. Add a direct unit test of `_make_recording_filenames` / `delete_replay_recordings` with `max_segment_id=None`.

findings.title: Assemble analytics event recorded before feature/validation checks
findings.body:
`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before body validation.

Every request is counted as an assemble event, including requests from orgs without the feature that get a 404 and requests with invalid bodies that get a 400. Polling requests are counted too. This inflates the metric.

Move the call after the feature check, and ideally after successful validation.
